A01:2021-Broken_Access_Control.name: Broken Access Control
A01:2021-Broken_Access_Control.description: Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data or performing a business function outside the user's limits.

A02:2021-Cryptographic_Failures.name: Cryptographic Failures
A02:2021-Cryptographic_Failures.description: Failures related to cryptography (or lack thereof) which often lead to exposure of sensitive data. Common issues include weak algorithms, improper key management, and transmitting data in cleartext.

A03:2021-Injection.name: Injection
A03:2021-Injection.description: Injection flaws occur when untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query. SQL, NoSQL, OS, and LDAP injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and template injection are all injection variants.

A04:2021-Insecure_Design.name: Insecure Design
A04:2021-Insecure_Design.description: Insecure design represents different weaknesses expressed as missing or ineffective control design. Secure design patterns and threat modeling are required to address this category.

A05:2021-Security_Misconfiguration.name: Security Misconfiguration
A05:2021-Security_Misconfiguration.description: The application might be vulnerable if it lacks appropriate security hardening, uses default credentials, exposes unnecessary features, or reveals error information to users.

A06:2021-Vulnerable_and_Outdated_Compone.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
A06:2021-Vulnerable_and_Outdated_Compone.description: Components such as libraries, frameworks, and other software modules run with the same privileges as the application. Using components with known vulnerabilities may undermine application defenses.

A07:2021-Identification_and_Authenticati.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
A07:2021-Identification_and_Authenticati.description: Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management is critical to protect against authentication-related attacks such as credential stuffing and brute force.

A08:2021-Software_and_Data_Integrity_Fai.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
A08:2021-Software_and_Data_Integrity_Fai.description: Code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations, including insecure deserialization, use of unsigned or unverified updates, CI/CD pipeline insecurity.

A09:2021-Security_Logging_and_Monitoring.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
A09:2021-Security_Logging_and_Monitoring.description: Without logging and monitoring, breaches cannot be detected. Insufficient logging, detection, monitoring, and active response occurs when auditable events are not logged correctly.

A10:2021-Server_Side_Request_Forgery.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
A10:2021-Server_Side_Request_Forgery.description: SSRF flaws occur whenever a web application fetches a remote resource without validating the user-supplied URL. It allows attackers to coerce the application to send crafted requests to unexpected destinations.
